baseline.equivalence_test: frozen QORE selection and baseline Generator output are unchanged on synthetic and collaborator screen fixtures

core_invariants: one Wiki-DPR retrieval and one frozen QORE K=5 selection per question
Answer Scorer, Generator, evaluator, labels, and retrieval depth remain unchanged
candidate generation and ranking receive no gold, evaluator, or post-hoc metric values
diagnostic outputs never feed select_passages or production Generator settings
compact artifacts contain no question, passage, candidate text, prediction, prompt, or evaluator trace

interfaces.input_schema: candidate mode IDs and runtime candidate strings plus question and selected context
interfaces.output_schema: candidate mode choice, scalar scores, parse status, timing, and reverse-order agreement
invariants: choice is keyed by stable candidate mode ID
score is deterministic under fixed model and tokenization

composition.merge_rule: all rankers consume the same immutable candidate set and emit mode-keyed scalar summaries; no ranker output changes candidate generation or selection

validation.baseline_equivalence: Phase 9I frozen baseline output and selection settings remain byte-equivalent at the compact scalar level

reproducibility.environment: auto-resolved compatible Python; NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct revision 53346005fb0ef11d3b6a83b12c895cca40156b6c; frozen DPR reader

limitations: This is an observation-only diagnostic and cannot establish a production method claim.
Candidate ranking and answer likelihood scoring have high nearest-work collision risk.
The reader support fallback is a diagnostic proxy when exact token span matching fails.
A screen null is inconclusive for a training-dependent idea, but this implementation has no learned training stage.
Any positive formal result still requires disjoint replication and a bounded novelty audit.
